method: Each angle is described by three SMPTE timecodes at the chosen rate: the clip in, the sync mark (a clap, flash or beep) and the clip out. Timecodes are compared as whole frame counts, so 24, 25, 30, 50 and 60 fps count straight through while 23.976, 29.97 and 59.94 use their exact 30000/1001-style rates for the seconds column. Drop-frame counting skips two frame numbers (four at 59.94) at every minute boundary except each tenth, which is why 00:01:00:00 has no meaning at 29.97 and is refused rather than shifted, and why a drop minute opens at 00:01:00:02 or 00:01:00:04. Every mark is aligned to sequence zero, so an angle's head trim is its mark minus its clip in and its tail trim is its clip out minus its mark. The shared window opens at the latest of those start offsets and closes at the earliest of the end offsets: the angle that opens latest limits the head and the angle that closes soonest limits the tail, and two angles that both begin or end exactly at their marks leave no shared frames, which is reported instead of a zero-length plan. The default three-angle 29.97 drop-frame example has A from 09:59:40:00 to 10:01:15:00 with its mark at 10:00:00:00, B from 14:22:58:00 to 14:24:05:00 with its mark at 14:23:11:07, and C from 01:04:52:24 to 01:06:10:00 with its mark at 01:05:00:12: head trims of 00:00:20:00, 00:00:13:05 and 00:00:07:16, tail trims of 00:01:15:00, 00:00:53:21 and 00:01:09:18, a shared window of 00:01:01:09 (1,837 frames, 61.29 s) that C limits at the head and B at the tail, and 00:03:59:02 of footage across the three clips. Seconds divide the exact frame count by the true rate, so they run a fraction past the timecode labels at 29.97. Names are limited to 24 characters, two to six angles are accepted, frames must sit inside their rate's range, and the mark must fall inside its clip; each refusal names the field and camera. Timecode labels are arithmetic only: camera clocks, genlock, drift and audio offset are not modelled, so marks are still worth checking on a slate or waveform. The page calculates locally and stores, uploads and transmits nothing.

sources.title: SMPTE ST 12-1 defines the time and control code format, including the drop-frame counting used at 29.97 and 59.94 fps.
Multicam editing aligns several camera recordings on a shared sync event so cuts can move between angles for as long as every angle has footage.
